angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 407,680 km at 49.72 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 20.1141 +/- 0.0207 mas (same row, RUWE 0.86): 49.72 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.586 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Triaud et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-80 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.450.2279T/abstract): 407,680 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.577 +/- 0.051 solar masses from Triaud et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-80 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.450.2279T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4143 +/- 92 K from Triaud et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-80 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.450.2279T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Triaud et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-80 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.450.2279T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-80.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.663, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-80 (pscomppars): spectral type K7-M0 V, from Salz et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015A&A...576A..42S/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-80 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.13 dex, from Triaud et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.450.2279T/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-80 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.03998, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-80 (pscomppars): age 7 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-80 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.27 km/s, from Triaud et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015MNRAS.450.2279T/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
